sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier medium-sized, head (except the pale broad band across the anterior 1/3 and the posterior margin) pale reddish wood-brown, nasus reddish wood-brown, antennae orange-yellow; posterior half of the head hemispherical, the anterior part narrowing and constricted; nasus long, about 3/4 of the head capsule, narrower, its width slightly variable; mandibles usually without pointed teeth; antennae usually 14-segmented, sometimes 13. The soldier resembles the larger of the two forms of E. pulleinei, differing mainly in head colour and in the shape of the nasus and antennae; E. pulleinei has 13-segmented antennae, whereas in this species 13 is exceptional. Queen medium-sized, very dark brown (almost black), very close to E. hastilis, differing in the darker body (especially postclypeus, antennae and labrum), the shorter postclypeus and the different antennal segmentation. The alate is not recorded in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Medium-sized. Head, except the pale broad band across the anterior 1/3 and the posterior margin, pale reddish wood-brown, nasus reddish wood-brown, antennae orange-yellow. Head, thorax and abdomen with very sparse short hairs. Posterior half of the head hemispherical, the anterior part narrowing and constricted; nasus long, about 3/4 of the head capsule, narrower, its width slightly variable; head shallower in profile, slightly concave behind the middle. Mandibles usually without pointed teeth. Antennae usually 14-segmented; segment 3 the shortest of all; segment 4 longer than segment 2; sometimes 13-segmented, in which case segment 4 is the shortest of all.
Measurements: body length 3.50—3.80 mm; head length (to apex of nasus) 1.51—1.65 mm; head width 0.79—0.88 mm; pronotum width 0.48—0.51 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Head with 4 broad dark ochraceous brown longitudinal stripes, each fading to pale brown at the sides, the vertex pale brown. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 longer than segment 2; segment 4 the shortest of all. Postclypeus slightly more than half as long as wide.
Measurements: body length 3.90—4.75 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.65 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.88 mm; head width 1.21 mm; pronotum width 0.74 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text:
Queen: a medium-sized, very dark brown (almost black) species. Very close to E. hastilis, differing in the darker body (especially postclypeus, antennae and labrum), the shorter postclypeus and the different antennal segmentation. Antennae (damaged): segments 2 and 3 about equal in length; segment 4 distinctly shorter than segments 2 and 3, the shortest of all. Postclypeus about half as long as wide.
Measurements: body length 14.00 mm; abdomen width 3.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.46 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.88 mm; head width 1.24 mm; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.33 mm; ocellus length 0.10 mm; pronotum length 0.62 mm; pronotum width 1.06 mm.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original reads Eutermes marcidus sp. nov., type locality Torres Strait: Banks Island, also recorded from Queensland: Mitchell River Mission Station (Cape York), Millungera. The alate is recorded in the original as "Not known", so no section is given for it; the original has a separate Queen section (antennae mutilated), placed under Other. The original describes the nest as a conical mound 12 inches wide at the base and 12 inches high, built in dry sandy soil; the nest contained well-developed nymphs and much chewed grass, and in the Mitchell River nest large nymphs reached as deep as 8 inches below the ground surface. OCR misreadings: "Pigs."/"Pig."="Figs."/"Fig.", "lahrum"="labrum", "pro-notom"="pronotum", "deadated"="dealated", "pulleine t"="pulleinei", "marocdus"="marcidus", "Eamitermes"="Hamitermes", "of rontal"="ofrontal".
